items.title: Pass the helped command's positional args to the help function (v2: strengthened oracle)
items.description: Supersedes cobra-2154. The behaviour asked for is unchanged: a help function installed with Command.SetHelpFunc(func(c *cobra.Command, args []string)) must receive the positional arguments of the command being helped, not the raw argument vector given to Execute (with -h/--help, or when a command without a Run is invoked) and not an empty slice (through the built-in `help` command). Issue: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/2154 (kind/bug, area/cobra-command, OPEN). Behaviour lives in the root `cobra` package, command.go: the flag.ErrHelp branch of (*Command).ExecuteC and the built-in help command in (*Command).InitDefaultHelpCmd. Why a v2: the independent review of the first delivery (PR #1 on the fork) found the cobra-2154 oracle weak, and the record confirms four gaps that let four different weak builds pass it. Gap 1, DisableFlagParsing: for a command with DisableFlagParsing cobra never parses its flags, so cmd.Flags().Args() is empty and a Run receives the raw remaining args (execute(): `argWoFlags = a`); the help function must receive those same raw args. Nothing in v1 asserted it, so the rework build (a 6-line change that passes cmd.Flags().Args() unconditionally in the ErrHelp branch and, in the help command, calls CheckErr(cmd.ParseFlags(remainingArgs)) then passes cmd.Flags().Args()) passed v1 while handing such a command an empty slice. Note the semantics: with DisableFlagParsing `-h` is not parsed either, so a runnable command gets `-h` in its Run and help is never shown; the help function is reached at the ErrHelp branch only when the command is not runnable (then `-h`, if given, is just another raw arg), and through `help <cmd> <args...>` for any command. Gap 2, flags through the help command: `root help sub --count 3 arg1` must reach the help function for `sub` with ["arg1"], sub's own flags and their values stripped exactly as `root sub --count 3 arg1 -h` does. At the base the built-in help command parses those flags as its own and Execute fails with `unknown flag: --count`; v1 never passed a flag through the help command, so build 1 (which forwards the help command's remaining args raw, from Find's second result) passed v1. Gap 3, shorthands and `--` through the help command: a hand-rolled token filter in the help command's Run (skip tokens starting with `--`, skip the next token when the flag has no NoOptDefVal, keep everything else) passed a draft of this oracle because the help-command path only exercised long-form flags. This oracle declares sub's flags with shorthands (`-c`, `-v`) and pins, through the help command, `-c 3 arg1`, `-v arg1`, grouped `-vc 3 arg1` (all -> ["arg1"]) and `arg1 -- -x` -> ["arg1" "-x"], mirrored on the -h path; and it pins that the tokens after the command path are parsed with the helped command's own flag set, not merely filtered out: after `help sub --count 7 arg1` sub's --count flag reads 7 inside the help function (a filter that drops the tokens leaves it at 0). Gap 4, the help command's own flags: a build that let the tokens through by no longer parsing the help command's own flags, and instead inspected its raw first token for `-h`/`--help`, passed a draft that pinned only `help -h`. Gap 5, hand-rolled help-command parsers: two further S-band builds (B', B'') that disable flag parsing on the help command and recognise a fixed set of first tokens (`-h`, `--help`, `--help=true`) passed a draft that pinned only those three spellings and `help --bogus`. The help command's own flags (and root's persistent flags, which every command inherits) that precede the topic keep their base behaviour, i.e. they are parsed by the help command exactly as pflag does, stated as observables on a fixture whose root declares the persistent flags --config (string) and --vroot/-V (bool): `help -h`, `help --help`, `help --help=true`, `help --help=1`, `help -V -h`, `help -Vh` and `help --vroot --help` each return nil from Execute and invoke the help function once for the help command itself (cmd.Name()=="help", args []), with root's --vroot reading true afterwards whenever it was given; `help -V sub arg1` and `help --config x sub arg1` return nil and invoke it once for "sub" with ["arg1"] (root's --vroot true in the first); and `help --bogus` returns a non-nil error from Execute with the help function not invoked. A help flag after the topic belongs to the helped command: `help sub -h` invokes the help function once for "sub" with [] (observed under the correct fix; at the base the help command parsed the `-h` as its own and showed help for the help command with the raw argument vector). Gap 6, a hand-rolled pflag re-implementation: a 35-line token walker on the help command (DisableFlagParsing on the help command, a loop over the leading `-` tokens that looks each one up in the help command's merged flag set, expands grouped shorthands, splits `--flag=value`, consumes the next token as the value of a value-taking flag, then checks the help flag and hands the rest to Find) passed the previous revision (40/40) while being wrong on base pflag behaviour. Four more observables, all green at the base (guards), pin the pflag behaviours such a walker gets wrong, on the same root-persistent-flags fixture: `help -- sub` returns nil and invokes the help function once for "sub" with [] (`--` before the topic ends the help command's flags; the walker rejects `--` as an unknown flag); `help --config= sub` returns nil and invokes it once for "sub" with [] with root's --config reading "" afterwards (`--config=` is the empty value and consumes nothing; the walker takes `sub` as the value and shows help for root); `help --config` (a value-taking flag as the last token) returns a non-nil error from Execute with the help function not invoked (the walker indexes past the end of argv and panics); `help -x` returns a non-nil error with the help function not invoked (the walker dereferences a nil *Flag from ShorthandLookup and panics). Root's --config is also asserted to read "x" after `help --config x sub arg1`. Under this oracle build 1 fails the five help-command flag cases, the parsed-flag-set case, the `help sub -h` case and the DisableFlagParsing-via-help-command case (10 ids with parents); the rework fails those, the `--` case (its CheckErr(ParseFlags) exits the test process on `-x` because the help command's own parser has already dropped the `--`) and both DisableFlagParsing ErrHelp cases (13 fail ids with parents plus the process exit); the raw-first-token build fails `help --help=true`, `help --help=1` and the three `-V`/`--vroot` help-command rows (help shown for root) and exits the test process at `help --bogus`; B' fails all six root-persistent-flag rows (it rejects `-V`, `-Vh`, `--vroot`, `--config` and `--help=1` as unknown flags) and B'' fails the four help-command-itself rows among them (help shown for root); the token-filter build fails the parsed-flag-set case; the hand-rolled walker fails `help -- sub` (unknown flag: --), `help --config= sub` (help shown for root, --config == "sub") and panics on `help --config` (index out of range) and `help -x` (nil pointer dereference) (6 ids with parents, per-leaf enumeration). The `--count=3 --verbose arg1` and `-v arg1` cases also reject making the help command merely tolerate unknown flags (FParseErrWhitelist), which would swallow `arg1` as the value of the bool flag. As before: the help function is invoked for the helped command, Execute returns nil, requesting help must not leave state behind that changes a later Execute on the same root, and the public API (SetHelpFunc, HelpFunc, Help signatures; Help() still passes []string{}) is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given root with a runnable subcommand `sub` (declaring an int flag --count with shorthand -c and a bool flag --verbose with shorthand -v) and a help function set via root.SetHelpFunc, executing `sub arg1 arg2 -h` invokes the help function exactly once with cmd.Name()=="sub" and args exactly ["arg1" "arg2"], and sub's Run does not execute.

Given the same tree, the help function receives exactly the positionals with every flag and flag value stripped: `sub -h arg1 arg2` -> ["arg1" "arg2"]; `sub --count 3 arg1 --help` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --count=3 arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --verbose arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub -c 3 arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub -v arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; and `--` ends flag parsing so `sub -h arg1 -- -x` -> ["arg1" "-x"].

Given `sub` without a Run (the issue's program), `sub arg1 arg2 -h` invokes the help function once for "sub" with ["arg1" "arg2"], and `sub arg1` (no help flag; help is shown because sub is not runnable) invokes it once for "sub" with ["arg1"].

Given the same tree, `help sub arg1 arg2` invokes the help function once with cmd.Name()=="sub" and args exactly ["arg1" "arg2"] (not an empty slice); with a child `nested` added to sub, `help sub nested arg1` invokes it once for "nested" with ["arg1"].
After `help sub arg1` on a root, executing `sub` on the same root runs sub's Run exactly once and does not invoke the help function again (the help command leaves no flag or argument state behind).
Execute returns a nil error in all of the above cases, and the help function is invoked for the helped command (not the root or the help command).

Given the same tree, `help sub --count 3 arg1` returns a nil error (the help command must not reject sub's flags as unknown flags of its own) and invokes the help function exactly once with cmd.Name()=="sub" and args exactly ["arg1"]; `help sub --count=3 --verbose arg1`, `help sub -c 3 arg1`, `help sub -v arg1` and `help sub -vc 3 arg1` likewise each invoke it once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1"] (the remaining args are parsed with sub's own flag set, so shorthands and grouped shorthands are stripped exactly as pflag does); `help sub arg1 -- -x` invokes it once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1" "-x"] (`--` ends flag parsing on this path too); after `help sub --count 7 arg1` the help function is invoked once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1"] and, inside that call, c.Flags().GetInt("count") on the helped command returns 7 with a nil error (and sub.Flags().GetInt("count") still returns 7 immediately after Execute); sub's Run does not execute in any of these cases.

Given `sub` with DisableFlagParsing=true and no Run, `sub arg1 --count 3` invokes the help function once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1" "--count" "3"] (the raw remaining args, as a Run would receive them; cmd.Flags().Args() is empty here and must not be used), and `sub -h arg1 --count 3` invokes it once for "sub" with exactly ["-h" "arg1" "--count" "3"] (with DisableFlagParsing the help flag is not parsed either; help is shown because sub is not runnable).

Given `sub` with DisableFlagParsing=true and a Run, `help sub arg1 --count 3` returns a nil error and invokes the help function once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1" "--count" "3"]; sub's Run does not execute.

The built-in help command's own flags (and root's persistent flags) that precede the topic keep their base behaviour, i.e. the help command parses them exactly as pflag does. Given root additionally declaring the persistent flags --config (string) and --vroot with shorthand -V (bool): `help -h`, `help --help`, `help --help=true`, `help --help=1`, `help -V -h`, `help -Vh` and `help --vroot --help` each return a nil error from Execute and, with the help function from the fixture installed, invoke it exactly once with cmd.Name()=="help" and args exactly [] (not for root, and not with the raw argument vector), sub's Run does not execute, and root.PersistentFlags().GetBool("vroot") reads true after each of the three `-V`/`--vroot` cases; `help -V sub arg1` returns a nil error and invokes the help function once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1"] with root's --vroot reading true afterwards, and `help --config x sub arg1` returns a nil error and invokes it once for "sub" with exactly ["arg1"]; root.PersistentFlags().GetString("config") reads "x" after `help --config x sub arg1`; `help -- sub` returns a nil error and invokes the help function once for "sub" with exactly [] (`--` before the topic ends the help command's flags); `help --config= sub` returns a nil error and invokes it once for "sub" with exactly [] and root.PersistentFlags().GetString("config") reads "" afterwards (`--config=` is the string flag set to the empty value and consumes no following token); `help --bogus`, `help --config` (a value-taking flag as the last token, no value) and `help -x` each return a non-nil error from Execute with the help function not invoked and sub's Run not executed; `completion bash -h` still shows the completion command's help (existing package tests TestHelpFlagOnHelpAndCompletionCommandsWithPersistentRequiredFlag and TestPluginWithSubCommands stay green).

A help flag after the topic belongs to the helped command, like every other token after the command path: `help sub -h` returns a nil error and invokes the help function exactly once with cmd.Name()=="sub" and args exactly [], and sub's Run does not execute.

All existing tests in the root `cobra` package and in `./doc` still pass (`go test -count=1 ./...`), `go vet ./` and `gofmt -l .` are clean, and the public API (SetHelpFunc, HelpFunc, Help signatures; Help() still passes []string{}) is unchanged.
structural_facts: reproduction: root := &cobra.Command{Use: "root"}; sub := &cobra.Command{Use: "sub", Run: func(*cobra.Command, []string) {}}; sub.Flags().IntP("count", "c", 0, ""); sub.Flags().BoolP("verbose", "v", false, ""); root.AddCommand(sub); root.SetHelpFunc(func(c *cobra.Command, args []string) { fmt.Printf("%s %q\n", c.Name(), args) }); root.SetArgs([]string{"sub", "arg1", "arg2", "-h"}); root.Execute() prints `sub ["sub" "arg1" "arg2" "-h"]`; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "sub", "arg1", "arg2"}); root.Execute() prints `sub []`; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "sub", "--count", "3", "arg1"}); root.Execute() returns the error `unknown flag: --count` (the help command parsed sub's flag as its own) and the help function is never called, so sub's --count stays 0; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "sub", "-c", "3", "arg1"}); root.Execute() returns `unknown shorthand flag: 'c' in -c`; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "sub", "arg1", "--", "-x"}); root.Execute() prints `sub []`; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "-h"}); root.Execute() prints `help ["help" "-h"]`, `help --help=true` prints `help ["help" "--help=true"]` and `help --help=1` prints `help ["help" "--help=1"]`; with root.PersistentFlags().String("config", "", "") and root.PersistentFlags().BoolP("vroot", "V", false, "") added: `help -V -h` prints `help ["help" "-V" "-h"]`, `help -Vh` prints `help ["help" "-Vh"]`, `help --vroot --help` prints `help ["help" "--vroot" "--help"]`, `help -V sub arg1` prints `sub []` and `help --config x sub arg1` prints `sub []`; root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "sub", "-h"}); root.Execute() prints `help ["help" "sub" "-h"]` (the help command parsed the `-h` as its own); root.SetArgs([]string{"help", "--bogus"}); root.Execute() returns the error `unknown flag: --bogus` without calling the help function (this is correct and must stay); likewise at the base, with the persistent flags declared, `help -- sub` prints `sub []` (`--` ends the help command's flags), `help --config= sub` prints `sub []` with root's --config == "", `help --config` returns the error `flag needs an argument: --config` and `help -x` returns the error `unknown shorthand flag: 'x' in -x`, the help function never called in the last two (all four are correct and must stay); with sub having no Run and DisableFlagParsing: true, root.SetArgs([]string{"sub", "arg1", "--count", "3"}); root.Execute() prints `sub ["sub" "arg1" "--count" "3"]`.

expected_behaviour: the help function receives the positional arguments of the helped command with the command path and all flags (and flag values, in `--flag value`, `--flag=value` and bool forms) removed and `--` honoured, in both the flag.ErrHelp branch of (*Command).ExecuteC (reached when --help is set and when the command is not runnable; the command's flags have already been parsed there, so cmd.Flags().Args() holds the positionals) and the `help <path to cmd> <args...>` path (the default help command's Run in (*Command).InitDefaultHelpCmd, where (*Command).Find(args) returns the command and its remaining args as its second result; those remaining args are the helped command's flags and positionals and must be parsed with the helped command's flag set, not rejected by the help command's own parser and not merely filtered out, so `help sub --count 3 arg1` -> ["arg1"], shorthands `-c 3`, `-v`, grouped `-vc 3` are stripped, `--` ends flag parsing (`help sub arg1 -- -x` -> ["arg1" "-x"]), and after `help sub --count 7 arg1` the helped command's --count reads 7 inside the help function); when the helped command has DisableFlagParsing its flags are never parsed (ParseFlags returns nil at once and cmd.Flags().Args() stays empty), so in both paths the help function must receive the raw remaining args unchanged, as (*Command).execute hands them to Run (`argWoFlags = a`); with DisableFlagParsing `-h` is not parsed either, so a runnable command never shows help and the ErrHelp branch is reached only for a non-runnable one; the help command's own flags (and root's persistent flags, inherited by the help command) that precede the topic keep their base behaviour, parsed by the help command exactly as pflag does: `help -h`, `help --help`, `help --help=true`, `help --help=1`, `help -V -h`, `help -Vh` and `help --vroot --help` reach the ErrHelp branch for the help command itself (the help function gets cmd.Name()=="help" and args [], Execute returns nil, root's --vroot reads true when given), `help -V sub arg1` and `help --config x sub arg1` reach the help function for "sub" with ["arg1"] (root's --vroot true in the first), `help -- sub` reaches the help function for "sub" with [] (`--` ends the help command's flags exactly as pflag does), `help --config= sub` reaches it for "sub" with [] and leaves root's --config == "" (the `=` form with an empty value consumes no following token), root's --config reads "x" after `help --config x sub arg1`, and `help --bogus`, `help --config` (value-taking flag without its value) and `help -x` (unknown shorthand) are non-nil errors from Execute with no help call, while the tokens from the topic onwards reach the helped command untouched, so a help flag after the topic is the helped command's (`help sub -h` -> help function for "sub" with []); requesting help must not mutate root's args; the helped command passed as the first parameter stays the same, and Help() keeps its signature and its []string{} argument.

exact_value: `sub arg1 arg2 -h` -> args ["arg1" "arg2"]; `sub -h arg1 arg2` -> ["arg1" "arg2"]; `sub --count 3 arg1 --help` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --count=3 arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub --verbose arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub -c 3 arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub -v arg1 -h` -> ["arg1"]; `sub -h arg1 -- -x` -> ["arg1" "-x"]; non-runnable sub: `sub arg1 arg2 -h` -> ["arg1" "arg2"], `sub arg1` -> ["arg1"]; `help sub arg1 arg2` -> ["arg1" "arg2"]; `help sub nested arg1` -> c.Name()=="nested", ["arg1"]; `help sub --count 3 arg1` -> nil error, ["arg1"]; `help sub --count=3 --verbose arg1` -> nil error, ["arg1"] (not [] — `arg1` is a positional, not the bool flag's value); `help sub -c 3 arg1` -> nil error, ["arg1"]; `help sub -v arg1` -> nil error, ["arg1"]; `help sub -vc 3 arg1` -> nil error, ["arg1"]; `help sub arg1 -- -x` -> nil error, ["arg1" "-x"]; `help sub --count 7 arg1` -> nil error, ["arg1"], and c.Flags().GetInt("count") == 7 (nil error) inside the help call and sub.Flags().GetInt("count") == 7 after Execute; `help -h` -> nil error, c.Name()=="help", []; `help --help` -> nil error, c.Name()=="help", []; `help --help=true` -> nil error, c.Name()=="help", []; `help --help=1` -> nil error, c.Name()=="help", []; with root's persistent flags --config (string) and --vroot/-V (bool) declared: `help -V -h` -> nil error, c.Name()=="help", [], root's --vroot == true after Execute; `help -Vh` -> same; `help --vroot --help` -> same; `help -V sub arg1` -> nil error, c.Name()=="sub", ["arg1"], root's --vroot == true; `help --config x sub arg1` -> nil error, c.Name()=="sub", ["arg1"], root's --config == "x" after Execute; `help -- sub` -> nil error, c.Name()=="sub", []; `help --config= sub` -> nil error, c.Name()=="sub", [], root's --config == "" after Execute; `help sub -h` -> nil error, c.Name()=="sub", []; `help --bogus` -> non-nil error, help function called 0 times; `help --config` -> non-nil error, help function called 0 times; `help -x` -> non-nil error, help function called 0 times; DisableFlagParsing non-runnable sub: `sub arg1 --count 3` -> ["arg1" "--count" "3"], `sub -h arg1 --count 3` -> ["-h" "arg1" "--count" "3"]; DisableFlagParsing runnable sub: `help sub arg1 --count 3` -> nil error, ["arg1" "--count" "3"]; after `help sub arg1` a following `sub` runs sub's Run once with the help function called 1 time in total; c.Name()=="sub", sub's Run not executed, and exactly one help-function call in every other case.
